dct_description_sm: This research focuses on the role natural disturbance agents and the implications they have on forest structure and processes. We are also investigating how these disturbances are responding to a changing climate and what implications this might have on the future of forests at the northern edge of their range. Using dendrochronology, past disturbance regimes of these forests will be reconstructed and the role of past disturbances on the present and future forests will be explored. The stability and reliance of these treeline ecotones will also be explored by examining the contributions from sexual and asexual recruitment into forest structure using a combination of ecological and genetic tools. By understanding the scale and intensity of disturbance regimes, we have knowledge of how sensitive and resilient these landscapes are to climate change.
dct_title_s: Dendrochronological, forest structure, and disturbance data from the Mealy Mountains, Labrador
